ip_top_stories.title: Delhi High Court Refuses Interim Injunction Against ChatGPT, Holds AI Training and Outputs Prima Facie Do Not Infringe Copyright – The Legal Affair
ip_top_stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has declined to grant ANI an interim injunction against OpenAI's ChatGPT, ruling that AI training on copyrighted content is prima facie protected under India's fair dealing doctrine. The court found that restraining ChatGPT would be detrimental to the growth of AI in India and against the public interest. The ruling represents India's first substantive judicial engagement with AI and copyright.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic agrees to $150mn copyright settlement over AI training
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic has agreed to a $150 million copyright settlement — reported elsewhere as $1.5 billion — with rights holders over the use of copyrighted material in AI training. The settlement has received court approval, though broader legal battles over AI training data continue across the industry.

ip_top_stories.title: Harry Potter publisher secures major payout in historic AI copyright case
ip_top_stories.summary: The publisher of the Harry Potter series has secured a significant financial settlement in what is being described as a historic AI copyright case. The case is notable as an early example of a major book publisher successfully obtaining compensation over the use of copyrighted works in AI training.

ip_top_stories.title: As GEMA awaits its Suno copyright verdict, the German collecting society launches 'PLAI' – a fully licensed dataset for training AI music tools
ip_top_stories.summary: Germany's GEMA collecting society has launched a fully licensed dataset called PLAI for training AI music tools, ahead of its pending copyright verdict against AI music generator Suno. The initiative represents an attempt to create a legitimate licensing pathway for AI training on musical works.

ip_top_stories.title: Music Publishers Canada Files to Intervene in Landmark AI and Copyright Federal Court Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Music Publishers Canada has filed to intervene in a landmark AI and copyright case before Canada's Federal Court. The move signals growing organised pushback from the publishing and music industry against AI companies' use of copyrighted material for training purposes.

ip_further_links.summary: A photographer failed to win a copyright claim after an AI-generated comic version of her image was produced, in a case that tests the boundaries of derivative works and AI output liability.

ip_further_links.summary: A South Korean startup is developing infrastructure to address the gap between AI music generation and copyright licensing, seeking to create systems that can handle rights management for AI-generated music.

ip_further_links.summary: Netflix has disclosed AI involvement in 300 of its titles, with the company noting that human creative input remains the determining factor for copyright ownership in AI-assisted productions.
